deities: Lord Shiva (small lingam at the entrance)

history.summary: Commissioned by Raoji Appaji Phanse (Fanse), Diwan of Baroda State during the reign of Govindrao Gaekwad, reportedly at the request of his wife Gulbadan, a Surya devotee - the Raopura locality itself is named after Raoji Appaji. Built in Nagar style of yellow stone on a raised platform in Surya Narayan Baug. A large stone elephant (identified as Airavat) stands at the entrance; legend says it was brought from a nearby hilltop stupa to block the Sun deity's direct gaze upon the city, deemed inauspicious. A small ancient Shivling stands beside the elephant's front leg. The sanctum's marble idol shows Surya riding a seven-horse chariot with consorts Sanjna and Chhaya; sunrise rays are said to enter the sanctum daily.

name: Shri Surya Narayan Temple
town_description: Vadodara (formerly Baroda) is a major city in Gujarat on the Vishwamitri river, famed as the cultural capital of the state. It was the seat of the Gaekwad rulers, whose patronage left palaces, museums and temples across the city. The Raopura area near the General Post Office is one of the old neighbourhoods of the city.

travel.road: Opposite the General Post Office / Raopura Post Office, in the city centre; city buses and auto-rickshaws reach it easily

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Rath Saptami (Magh) for the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-7:00 PM with morning and evening aarti (single source - verify). Photography inside is reported to be restricted or prohibited.
